Let $\pi:E\to M$ be a smooth rank-$r$ vector bundle and let
$\Phi_\alpha:\pi^{-1}(U_\alpha)\to U_\alpha\times\mathbb R^r$ be a local
trivialization whose restriction on each fibre is a linear isomorphism. The
pair $(U_\alpha,\Phi_\alpha)$ is a **vector bundle chart**.

For two vector bundle charts $(U_\alpha,\Phi_\alpha)$ and
$(U_\beta,\Phi_\beta)$, the overlap map

$$\Phi_\beta\circ\Phi_\alpha^{-1}:(U_\alpha\cap U_\beta)\times\mathbb R^r\to (U_\alpha\cap U_\beta)\times\mathbb R^r$$

has the form

$$\Phi_\beta\circ\Phi_\alpha^{-1}(p,v)=(p,g_{\beta\alpha}(p)v),$$

where $g_{\beta\alpha}:U_\alpha\cap U_\beta\to GL(r,\mathbb R)$ is smooth. The
map $g_{\beta\alpha}$ is the **transition function** from chart $\alpha$ to
chart $\beta$.

Let $M$ be a smooth manifold and let $(U_i)_{i\in I}$ be an open cover of $M$. A family of smooth functions $(\phi_i)_{i\in I}$ with $\phi_i:M\to [0,1]$ is a **smooth partition of unity subordinate to** $(U_i)_{i\in I}$ when:

1. the family $(\operatorname{supp}(\phi_i))_{i\in I}$ is locally finite;
2. $\operatorname{supp}(\phi_i)\subseteq U_i$ for every $i\in I$; and
3. $\sum_i \phi_i(p)=1$ for every $p\in M$.

derivations.claim: Choose a finite bundle atlas and a subordinate finite smooth partition of unity using compactness and [F1, F2]. In each chart multiply a section coefficient by its partition function, extend by zero within the chart, convolve with a fixed compactly supported smooth mollifier of radius $\delta$, and sum the finitely many resulting local sections. For each $\delta>0$ this defines a linear operator $S_\delta:C^0(M,E)\to\Gamma^\infty(E)$: every output derivative is an integral of the input against a derivative of a fixed smooth kernel, so each $C^r$ seminorm is bounded by a finite constant times the input $C^0$ norm. Uniform continuity of each input on compact chart supports gives $\|S_\delta u-u\|_{C^0}\to0$ for every $u$. Since $x\mapsto s(x,\cdot)$ has compact image in $C^0(M,E)$, a finite subcover argument makes this convergence uniform over $x\in X$.

The family $x\mapsto S_\delta s(x,\cdot)$ is continuous into $C^\infty$ by the seminorm bounds in step 1.1. On a collar $c:K\times[0,2a)\to X$, write $r(c(k,t))=k$ and choose a continuous cutoff $\chi$ equal to $1$ at $t=0$ and supported in $t<a$. Set
$$s_1(x)=S_\delta s(x)+\chi(x)\bigl(s(r(x))-S_\delta s(r(x))\bigr)$$
on the collar and $s_1=S_\delta s$ off it. Every term is a smooth section in $m$ and varies continuously in $C^\infty$ with $x$. At $x\in K$, $s_1(x)=s(x)$. As $x$ approaches $K$, continuity into $C^0$ and the uniform approximation in step 1.1 make the correction uniformly small; choose the collar width and then $\delta$ so $s_1$ remains arbitrarily $C^0$-close to $s$.

For each marked point choose a bundle chart and a smooth bump $b_i$ supported in that chart with $b_i(m_i)=1$; shrink the charts to be pairwise disjoint. In the chart extend $v_i-s_1(x,m_i)$ as the constant coefficient vector and multiply by $b_i$. The resulting correction $c_i(x,\cdot)$ is a smooth section continuous in $x$ in every $C^r$ seminorm, is zero on $K$ because $s_1=s=v_i$ there, and changes the value at $m_i$ by exactly $v_i-s_1(x,m_i)$. Put $\widetilde s=s_1+\sum_i c_i$. The finite corrections preserve $C^\infty$ continuity and the relative condition. Since the errors at the marked points are bounded by the uniform $C^0$ error from step 2.1 and the bumps have fixed bounded norms, choosing that error sufficiently small gives the prescribed $\varepsilon$ bound.

For $0\le t\le1$ define $H_t(x,m)=(1-t)s(x,m)+t\widetilde s(x,m)$ in the vector space $E_m$. This is continuous, equals $s$ at $t=0$ and $\widetilde s$ at $t=1$, and is constant on $K$ and at each marked point because both endpoint families agree there. Thus the required relative homotopy exists.

For a well-pointed CGWH based space $(X,x_0)$ set
$$CX=(X\times I)/(X\times\{1\}\cup\{x_0\}\times I),\qquad \Sigma X=CX/(X\times\{0\}).$$
The common collapsed set is the basepoint; the copy of X at height zero is the cone base. All products and mapping conventions are those of [[def-compactly-generated-conventions-for-based-homotopy]], and well-pointedness means [[def-cofibration-and-homotopy-extension-property]].

For a based $f:X\to Y$ put $C_f=Y\cup_f CX$, the **reduced homotopy cofiber**, with $i:Y\to C_f$ the inclusion and $q:C_f\to\Sigma X$ collapsing Y. This reduced notation is used in this item and its based consumers; it differs from the unreduced cone of [[def-mapping-cylinder-and-mapping-cone]]. A reduced cylinder also collapses the basepoint track. Maps on all these quotients are defined by [[thm-quotient-universal-property]].

Write $\rho_X([x,t])=[x,1-t]$ and $-\Sigma f=\rho_Y\Sigma f$. The cofiber sequence convention is
$$X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{i}C_f\xrightarrow{q}\Sigma X\xrightarrow{-\Sigma f}\Sigma Y\xrightarrow{-\Sigma i}\Sigma C_f\xrightarrow{-\Sigma q}\Sigma^2X\xrightarrow{\Sigma^2 f}\Sigma^2Y\longrightarrow\cdots.$$
The homotopy equivalences and mapping-set exactness behind this notation are proved below; this definition does not assert a covariant exact sequence of homotopy groups.

For a space $X$ and commutative unital coefficient ring $R$, put
$$H^*(X;R)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}H^n(X;R),\qquad [\varphi]\smile[\psi]=[\varphi\smile\psi].$$
The groups and equality of representatives are those of [[def-singular-cohomology-with-coefficients]]. The multiplication descends through both quotient maps by [[thm-cup-product-leibniz-identity]], including simultaneous changes. Extend to finite sums of homogeneous classes by distributivity; only finitely many summands occur, so each product belongs to the displayed direct sum.

This is the **singular cohomology ring**. To check the ring assertion before using it, let $\varphi,\psi,\eta$ have degrees $p,q,r$. On an arbitrary $(p+q+r)$-simplex both parenthesizations of their cochain cup product evaluate to
$$\varphi(\sigma[0,\ldots,p])\,\psi(\sigma[p,\ldots,p+q])\,\eta(\sigma[p+q,\ldots,p+q+r]).$$
Restriction to a face and then a face of that face is restriction to the listed vertex block, and multiplication in $R$ is associative. Thus cochain associativity holds exactly and descends to classes. Bilinearity gives the two distributive laws. Addition, additive inverses and zero come from the abelian quotient groups. Products of degrees $p,q$ have degree $p+q$.

Its multiplicative unit is the class of the cochain $\mathbf1\in C^0(X;R)$ assigning $1_R$ to every singular vertex. On any edge, $\delta\mathbf1=1_R-1_R=0$. The front/back formula gives $\mathbf1\smile\varphi=\varphi=\varphi\smile\mathbf1$ on every simplex. This includes all components at once: degree-zero cochains need not have finite support on the set of vertices or components.

If $X$ is empty or $R=0$, the ring is the zero ring and its unit equals zero, as allowed by our unital-ring convention. The formula for three factors works also when any degree is zero and for degenerate simplices; for one-point $X$ it has the same unit. Nothing here chooses a representative for every class: the quotient operation is defined by representative independence. No AC is used.

Assume AC. For a CW pair $(X,A)$ and local system $\mathcal L$, the cellular cochain complex obtained from the skeletal filtration computes singular cohomology with local coefficients:
$$H^n\bigl(C^*_{\mathrm{cell}}(X,A;\mathcal L)\bigr)\cong H^n(X,A;\mathcal L).$$
For a connected pair, it is the equivariant-Hom complex on cellular chains after the published right chain action is converted to the left action $g\cdot c=c\cdot g^{-1}$; equivalently its cochains satisfy $\varphi(c\cdot g)=g^{-1}\varphi(c)$. The comparison is natural for cellular maps with correctly directed coefficient morphisms.

derivations.claim: By [F1], the cells of $C_f$ have dimensions $0,2,4$. Its cellular cochain groups are therefore $\mathbb Z$ in those degrees and zero in degrees $1$ and $3$; every cellular coboundary into or out of degrees $2$ and $4$ is zero because the adjacent cochain group is zero. [F3] gives $H^2(C_f;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z$ and $H^4(C_f;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z$, with the restriction and oriented top-cell generators in the Definition.

By [F2], $x\smile x$ belongs to $H^4(C_f;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z y$. Since $y$ is a generator, there is a unique integer $H(f)$ with $x\smile x=H(f)y$. The orientations fix its sign, so the displayed equation defines an integer without any further choice.

The quotient projection

$$p:\mathbb R\longrightarrow\mathbb R/\mathbb Z,\qquad t\longmapsto[t],$$

is a universal covering space of the quotient circle, pointed by $0\mapsto[0]$.

Let $Y$ be path-connected and locally path-connected, let $f:(Y,y_0)\to(B,b_0)$ be based, and let $p:(E,e_0)\to(B,b_0)$ be a covering. A based lift $\widetilde f:(Y,y_0)\to(E,e_0)$ exists if and only if $f_*\pi_1(Y,y_0)\subseteq p_*\pi_1(E,e_0)$; when it exists it is unique.

For a based Serre fibration $p:(E,e_0)\to(B,b_0)$ with fiber $F=p^{-1}(b_0)$, the sequence
$$\cdots\to\pi_n(F)\xrightarrow{i_*}\pi_n(E)\xrightarrow{p_*}\pi_n(B)\xrightarrow{\partial_p}\pi_{n-1}(F)\to\cdots\to\pi_1(B)\xrightarrow{\partial_p}\pi_0(F)\xrightarrow{i_*}\pi_0(E)\xrightarrow{p_*}\pi_0(B)$$
is exact wherever there is an incoming and outgoing arrow. Basepoints are $e_0,b_0$ as appropriate. Exactness means incoming image equals the inverse image of the distinguished element. Arrows are homomorphisms where both group structures are defined; the component terms are pointed sets. The last arrow is onto precisely when $p(E)$ meets every path component of $B$.

There is a right action of $\pi_1(B,b_0)$ on $\pi_0(F)$: $[e]\cdot[\gamma]$ is the endpoint component of a lift of $\gamma$ starting at $e$, with loop products traversed left-to-right. Its orbits are precisely the fibers of $i_*:\pi_0(F)\to\pi_0(E)$, and the stabilizer of $[e_0]$ is $p_*\pi_1(E,e_0)$. Our boundary convention gives $\partial_p[\gamma]=[e_0]\cdot[\gamma]^{-1}$. These assertions require no AC.

For every r≥1, degree is an isomorphism $\pi_r(S^r,b)\to\mathbb Z$, sending the identity to +1 and cubical concatenation, equivalently oriented pinch sum, to addition. Two based sphere self-maps are homotopic through based maps if and only if their degrees agree. No infinite choice principle is needed.

Assume AC. For every $N\geq0$ identify
$\mathbb{CP}^N=\operatorname{Gr}_1(\mathbb C^{N+1})$, the space of complex
lines in $\mathbb C^{N+1}$, and let $\gamma$ be the tautological complex line
with $x=e(\gamma_{\mathbb R})\in H^2(\mathbb{CP}^N;\mathbb Z)$ its Euler class
in the complex orientation. Then, as a graded ring,
$$H^*(\mathbb{CP}^N;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z[x]/(x^{N+1}),$$
the class $x$ generating each even degree and the odd groups vanishing; for
$0\leq m\leq N$ the standard inclusion
$\mathbb{CP}^m\hookrightarrow\mathbb{CP}^N$, induced by
$\mathbb C^{m+1}\subseteq\mathbb C^{N+1}$, pulls $x$ back to $x$.

Let $f:S^3\to S^2$ be a based continuous map. Give $S^2$ an orientation and give the attached $4$-cell its chosen orientation. Its mapping cone is the CW complex $C_f=S^2\cup_fD^4$, with the basepoint as its $0$-cell. Let $x\in H^2(C_f;\mathbb Z)$ be the unique class restricting to the positive generator of $H^2(S^2;\mathbb Z)$, and let $y\in H^4(C_f;\mathbb Z)$ be the generator determined by the oriented $4$-cell. Define the integral mapping-cone Hopf invariant $H(f)\in\mathbb Z$ by the equation
$$x\smile x=H(f)y.$$

derivations.claim: The Hopf map is a locally trivial circle bundle: over the chart $z_0\ne0$ its fiber coordinate is the phase of $z_0$, and over $z_1\ne0$ it is the phase of $z_1$; these charts cover $\mathbb{CP}^1$. Hence it is a Serre fibration. By [F1], $\pi_2(S^1)=\pi_3(S^1)=0$; the LES [F2] therefore makes $h_*:\pi_3(S^3)\to\pi_3(S^2)$ an isomorphism. By [F3] its source is generated by the identity, so $[h]$ generates $\pi_3(S^2)\cong\mathbb Z$.

Write $\mathbb{CP}^2=\{[z_0:z_1:z_2]\}$ and use the open cell $z_2\ne0$ with representative $(w_0,w_1,1)$, $w\in\mathbb C^2$. Its characteristic disk can be taken as the unit ball in $\mathbb C^2$ via $w\mapsto[w_0:w_1:\sqrt{1-|w|^2}]$; the interior parametrizes the complement of $\mathbb{CP}^1$, and on $|w|=1$ the boundary map is $[w_0:w_1]=h(w)$. Thus $\mathbb{CP}^2$ is the mapping cone $C_h$. By [F4], the degree-two generator squares to the degree-four generator, so [F5] gives $H(h)=1$.

Let $d_m:S^3\to S^3$ have degree $m$. The radial cone extension $D^4\to D^4$, $ru\mapsto r d_m(u)$, has relative degree $m$ and boundary $d_m$. Together with the identity on $S^2$, it defines a map $C_{h\circ d_m}\to C_h$, since the boundary attaching maps agree. It pulls the degree-two generator of $C_h$ back to that of $C_{h\circ d_m}$ and the degree-four generator back to $m$ times the latter. Pulling back $x_h^2=y_h$ therefore gives $x_{h\circ d_m}^2=m y_{h\circ d_m}$, which is exactly $H(h\circ d_m)=m$ by [F5].

$$(a\otimes b)(a'\otimes b')=(-1)^{|b||a'|}(a\smile a')\otimes(b\smile b').$$
For arbitrary spaces $X,Y$, external product $a\times b=\operatorname{pr}_X^*a\smile\operatorname{pr}_Y^*b$ gives a unital graded-ring homomorphism to $H^*(X\times Y;R)$. This multiplicativity requires no AC.

Assume in addition AC, that $R$ is a PID, and that either every $H_q(Y;R)$ or every $H_p(X;R)$ is finite free over $R$. Then this homomorphism is an isomorphism.

For CW pairs $(X,A),(Y,B)$ with supplied characteristic maps, relative external product is likewise a graded-ring homomorphism
$$H^*(X,A;R)\mathbin{\widehat\otimes}_R H^*(Y,B;R)\longrightarrow H^*(X\times Y,(A\times Y)\cup(X\times B);R),$$
where the hat denotes the displayed graded multiplication on the ordinary graded direct-sum tensor product, not a completion. Relative rings need not have units. This relative multiplicativity is choice-free for every commutative unital $R$. Under AC and the PID hypothesis it is an isomorphism if either every $H_q(Y,B;R)$ or every $H_p(X,A;R)$ is finite free. Neither additive assertion requires bounded dimension or finite-rank singular chain groups. Products have their ordinary product topologies; AC enters only in additive bijectivity.

Let $\iota_1,\iota_2:\Sigma Z\to\Sigma Z\vee\Sigma Z$ be the wedge inclusions. The reduced suspension pinch map $p_Z:\Sigma Z\to\Sigma Z\vee\Sigma Z$ is induced by
$$p_Z([z,t])=\begin{cases}\iota_1([z,2t]),&0\le t\le\tfrac12,\\\iota_2([z,2t-1]),&\tfrac12\le t\le1.\end{cases}$$
At $t=\tfrac12$ both values are the wedge basepoint.

The map $\nabla:W\to S^2$ extends over the cone on $\beta$ by the definition $\beta=\nabla\alpha$; hence it extends to a map $q:S^2\times S^2=W\cup_\alpha D^4\to C_\beta$. On $W$, $q$ is the fold into the bottom $S^2$ of $C_\beta$, so $q^*x=a+b$. On the open $4$-cell, the extension is the characteristic disk of $C_\beta$ with degree $+1$ by [A1], so $q^*y=ab$.

$$r=(\Sigma p_1\vee\Sigma p_2)\circ\operatorname{pinch}:\Sigma(S^2\times S^2)\longrightarrow\Sigma S^2\vee\Sigma S^2,$$

Composing with $\Sigma\nabla$ gives $\Sigma\beta\simeq *$. By the definition of the suspension homomorphism, this is $2[\Sigma h]=0$ because $[\beta]=2[h]$ from step 2.1 and [F1] identifies $[h]$ as the generator.

A **locally trivial fiber bundle with fiber $F$** is a continuous map $p:E\to B$, an open cover $(U_i)_{i\in S}$ of $B$, and homeomorphisms
$$\theta_i:p^{-1}(U_i)\longrightarrow U_i\times F,\qquad \operatorname{pr}_1\theta_i=p|_{p^{-1}(U_i)}.$$
Here bundle charts, including those used later for principal and associated bundles, are charts in ordinary topological spaces with ordinary product and subspace topologies. A bundle whose spaces are CGWH in addition can be considered in the CGWH fibration convention; we do not silently replace an ordinary product chart by a weaker k-product-chart assumption. Products and homeomorphisms have the meanings of [[thm-product-universal-property]] and [[def-homeomorphism-and-open-maps]].

On $U_i\cap U_j$, the coordinate change has the form $(b,x)\mapsto(b,g_{ji}(b,x))$, with continuous inverse $(b,y)\mapsto(b,g_{ij}(b,y))$. In particular each $g_{ji}(b,-)$ is a homeomorphism of $F$. The identities $g_{ii}(b,x)=x$ and $g_{ki}(b,x)=g_{kj}(b,g_{ji}(b,x))$ hold because the corresponding chart composites cancel. No topology on a homeomorphism group of $F$ is assumed.

The bundle is **numerable** when the data include a partition $(\rho_i:B\to[0,1])_{i\in S}$ with locally finite cozero sets, sum one, and
$$\operatorname{supp}(\rho_i)=\overline{\{b:\rho_i(b)>0\}}\subseteq U_i.$$
This is the support-subordinate convention of [[def-partition-of-unity-subordinate-to-a-cover]]. Repeating a chart with multiple indices is allowed, so a partition subordinate to a refinement can be accompanied by an explicitly assigned original chart. Merely having pointwise finite sums or cozero containment is not this specified numerating data.

An empty base forces $E$ empty and allows the empty cover and partition. The fiber $F$ may be empty: then every chart domain, hence $E$, is empty even when $B$ is nonempty. When $F$ is nonempty the charts imply surjectivity by taking one point in the chart fiber for each particular base point; this assertion does not require choosing a simultaneous section. Over a point a chart identifies $E$ with $F$. No AC is assumed in the definition.

Assume AC. Every numerable fiber bundle, with its supplied ordinary local product charts and support-subordinate locally finite partition of unity, is a Hurewicz fibration in all ordinary spaces. In particular a bundle of CGWH spaces with these charts is a Hurewicz fibration in CGWH. AC is used to well-order the set of finite chart words. No selection of a chart for every base point or of a separate lift for every path is made.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Let $M$ be a smooth manifold and let $(U_i)_{i\in I}$ be an open cover of $M$. A family of smooth functions $(\phi_i)_{i\in I}$ with $\phi_i:M\to [0,1]$ is a **smooth partition of unity subordinate to** $(U_i)_{i\in I}$ when:

1. the family $(\operatorname{supp}(\phi_i))_{i\in I}$ is locally finite;
2. $\operatorname{supp}(\phi_i)\subseteq U_i$ for every $i\in I$; and
3. $\sum_i \phi_i(p)=1$ for every $p\in M$.

derivations.claim: Fix $v_0\in S^{2N-1}$. Choose an orthonormal basis $w_1,\ldots,w_{N-1}$ of $v_0^\perp$ so the matrix $(w_1,\ldots,w_{N-1},v_0)$ has determinant $1$. For $v$ in a sufficiently small neighborhood $U$ of $v_0$, project each $w_i$ onto $v^\perp$ and apply Gram–Schmidt in that fixed order. The projected vectors remain linearly independent after shrinking $U$, because their Gram determinant is continuous and equals $1$ at $v_0$. The resulting orthonormal frame depends smoothly on $v$. Multiply its first vector by the inverse of the determinant of the frame if necessary; this scalar has modulus one and the adjustment is smooth, preserves orthonormality, and makes the determinant exactly one. Thus $s(v)\in SU(N)$ is a smooth local section of $p$ on $U$.

For $g\in p^{-1}(U)$ with last column $v$, the matrix $s(v)^{-1}g$ fixes the last basis vector. Unitarity makes its orthogonal complement invariant, so it is block diagonal $\operatorname{diag}(A,1)$; determinant one gives $A\in SU(N-1)$. The maps
$$(A,v)\longmapsto s(v)\operatorname{diag}(A,1),\qquad g\longmapsto(\operatorname{upperBlock}(s(p(g))^{-1}g),p(g))$$
are smooth inverses between $SU(N-1)\times U$ and $p^{-1}(U)$. This proves local triviality with the asserted fiber.

The sphere is compact, so finitely many such neighborhoods cover it; [F2] gives a smooth partition of unity and hence a numeration. Applying [F1] proves the bundle is a Hurewicz fibration. For $N=2$, the stabilizer of the last column in $SU(2)$ has its upper block in $SU(1)=\{1\}$, so the fiber is a point.

For a based Serre fibration $p:(E,e_0)\to(B,b_0)$ with fiber $F=p^{-1}(b_0)$, the sequence

is exact wherever there is an incoming and outgoing arrow. Basepoints are $e_0,b_0$ as appropriate. Exactness means incoming image equals the inverse image of the distinguished element. Arrows are homomorphisms where both group structures are defined; the component terms are pointed sets. The last arrow is onto precisely when $p(E)$ meets every path component of $B$.

There is a right action of $\pi_1(B,b_0)$ on $\pi_0(F)$: $[e]\cdot[\gamma]$ is the endpoint component of a lift of $\gamma$ starting at $e$, with loop products traversed left-to-right. Its orbits are precisely the fibers of $i_*:\pi_0(F)\to\pi_0(E)$, and the stabilizer of $[e_0]$ is $p_*\pi_1(E,e_0)$. Our boundary convention gives $\partial_p[\gamma]=[e_0]\cdot[\gamma]^{-1}$. For integers $0\le k<r$, $r\ge1$, every continuous based map $(S^k,a)\to(S^r,b)$ is nullhomotopic through maps fixing a. For k=0 this says every point of $S^r$ can be joined to b. No arbitrary choice principle is required.

For every r≥1, degree is an isomorphism $\pi_r(S^r,b)\to\mathbb Z$, sending the identity to +1 and cubical concatenation, equivalently oriented pinch sum, to addition. Two based sphere self-maps are homotopic through based maps if and only if their degrees agree. No infinite choice principle is needed.

Let $(X,x_0)$ be a based CW complex that is $(n-1)$-connected, where $n\ge1$. Let $\Sigma X=C_+X\cup_X C_-X$ be its unreduced two-cone suspension, based at the lower cone point $p_-$. The suspension homomorphism
$$E:\pi_i(X,x_0)\longrightarrow\pi_{i+1}(\Sigma X,p_-),\qquad [h]\longmapsto[\Sigma h],$$
where the source sphere is also suspended by the two-cone construction and based at its lower cone point, is an isomorphism for $1\le i<2n-1$ and a surjection for $i=2n-1$. In degree zero both $\pi_0(X)$ and $\pi_1(\Sigma X)$ are singletons, so the corresponding pointed map is a bijection. The theorem and these precise basepoint conventions require no choice principle. No endpoint injectivity is asserted.

Let $h:S^3\to\mathbb{CP}^1\cong S^2$ be the Hopf map $h(z_0,z_1)=[z_0:z_1]$ on the unit sphere in $\mathbb C^2$. Then $h$ generates $\pi_3(S^2)\cong\mathbb Z$. With the complex orientations, $C_h\cong\mathbb{CP}^2$, $H(h)=1$, and for every integer $m$ and degree-$m$ map $d_m:S^3\to S^3$, $H(h\circ d_m)=m$.

Give $S^2\times S^2$ its product CW structure with $2$-skeleton $W=S^2\vee S^2$ and one oriented $4$-cell attached by $\alpha:S^3\to W$. Let $\nabla:W\to S^2$ fold the two oriented summands by the identity and put $\beta=\nabla\circ\alpha$. For a based map $f:S^3\to S^2$, its integral Hopf invariant $H(f)$ is defined by $x^2=H(f)y$ in the mapping cone $C_f=S^2\cup_fD^4$, where $x$ and $y$ are the positive generators of $H^2(C_f;\mathbb Z)$ and $H^4(C_f;\mathbb Z)$. Consequently, if $\eta_3=\Sigma h$ is the suspension of the Hopf generator, then $2[\eta_3]=0$ in $\pi_4(S^3)$.

The nonzero composite $\eta_3\circ\eta_4$ in [F5] implies $\eta_3\ne0$, since a composite with a null factor is null. Thus the cyclic quotient generated by $\eta_3$ has exactly two elements, proving $\pi_4(SU(2))\cong\mathbb Z/2$; the same nonzero composite lies in $\pi_5(S^3)$, so that group is nonzero.

Induct on $N\ge3$. The base sphere $S^{2N-1}$ has dimension at least five, so [F3] makes its homotopy groups in degrees $1,2,3,4$ zero. The component exact sequence and the connected fiber and base show $SU(N)$ is path connected: the map on components is onto, and its kernel is the image of the one-point component set of the fiber. Starting from [step 1.1], induction gives all three displayed low groups and connectedness for every $N$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a compact, connected, oriented, boundaryless smooth manifold of dimension $d\in\{3,4\}$ with a smooth Riemannian metric, let $N\ge2$, and fix a smooth right principal $SU(N)$-bundle $\pi:P\to M$, a smooth connection $A_0$, and a point $p_m\in P$ over $x_m\in M$. Use the standard unitary representation of $SU(N)$ on $\mathbb C^N$ and the invariant positive inner product $\langle X,Y\rangle=-\operatorname{tr}(XY)$ on $\mathfrak{su}(N)$. Define the adjoint vector bundle $\operatorname{ad}P=P\times_{\operatorname{Ad}}\mathfrak{su}(N)$ and the adjoint group bundle $\operatorname{Ad}P=P\times_{\operatorname{Ad}}SU(N)$ with associated-bundle relation $[pg,z]=[p,\operatorname{Ad}_g z]$.

Choose one finite smooth bundle atlas with relatively compact coordinate domains and a subordinate partition of unity. For each integer $k>d/2+1$, let $H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$ and $H^{k+1}(\operatorname{ad}P)$ be the Sobolev completions of smooth sections in the resulting finite-atlas norms. Define the affine configuration space $\mathcal A_k:=A_0+H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$ and the set $\mathcal G_{k+1}:=H^{k+1}(\operatorname{Ad}P)$ of Sobolev gauge sections. The next lemma proves that the pointwise product and inverse close on this set and make it a Hilbert Lie group. Its based subset is $\mathcal G_{k+1,m}:=\{u\in\mathcal G_{k+1}:u(p_m)=e\}$. Let $Z_N=\{zI_N:z^N=1\}$ be the center of $SU(N)$, viewed as constant gauge sections. Indeed, if $Z=(z_{ij})$ is central and $D=\operatorname{diag}(t_1,\ldots,t_N)\in SU(N)$, then $(t_j-t_i)z_{ij}=0$. For each $i\ne j$ one can choose such a diagonal matrix with $t_i\ne t_j$, so $Z$ is diagonal. Commuting with the determinant-one unitary rotation whose block on the $(i,j)$ coordinates is $\begin{pmatrix}\cos t&\sin t\\-\sin t&\cos t\end{pmatrix}$ for $t\notin\pi\mathbb Z$ forces the $i$th and $j$th diagonal entries equal. Hence $Z=zI_N$; determinant one gives $z^N=1$, and conversely every such scalar is central. Write $\bar{\mathcal G}_{k+1}$ for the set of $Z_N$-cosets with quotient topology; the next lemma also verifies that the induced pointwise operation makes it a Hilbert Lie group.

Let $\mathcal A_\infty:=A_0+\Omega^1(M,\operatorname{ad}P)$ and let $\mathcal G_\infty$ be the smooth gauge group, with the $C^\infty$ section topology generated by all finite-atlas derivative seminorms. Define $\bar{\mathcal G}_\infty:=\mathcal G_\infty/Z_N$. In a local section of $P$, write a connection as a matrix-valued one-form $A$ and a gauge section as a map $u$ into $SU(N)$; the right gauge action is $A^u:=u^{-1}Au+u^{-1}du$, equivalently pullback by the gauge automorphism associated with $u$. The calculus lemma proves that this formula defines a smooth action on the Sobolev spaces above. For an adjoint section $\xi$, set $d_A\xi:=d\xi+[A,\xi]$ using the degree-one Lie-algebra-valued-form bracket. In local coordinates and an orthonormal adjoint frame, define the formal adjoint on an adjoint-valued one-form $a$ by $(d_A^*a)=-g^{ij}(\nabla_i^{\mathrm{LC}}a_j+[A_i,a_j])$, where $\nabla^{\mathrm{LC}}$ differentiates the covector index. This is the $L^2$ adjoint for the Riemannian volume and stated fiber metric; its local coefficient formula defines a distribution at Sobolev regularity.

For $A\in\mathcal A_k$, parallel transport of its $C^1$ connection form around piecewise smooth loops based at $p_m$ defines a subgroup $\operatorname{Hol}_{p_m}(A)\subseteq SU(N)$. Call $A$ irreducible when this subgroup leaves no nonzero proper complex subspace of $\mathbb C^N$ invariant; changing the chosen frame conjugates the subgroup and leaves this condition unchanged. Write $\mathcal A_k^*$ and $\mathcal A_\infty^*$ for the irreducible loci. Once the calculus lemma verifies the group action, define orbit equivalence by $A\sim B$ exactly when $B=A^u$ for some gauge section $u$; all resulting quotients carry the quotient topology, whose open sets are those with open inverse image under the orbit projection.

Let $X$ be a compact finite-dimensional smooth manifold, $K\subseteq X$ a closed smooth submanifold with a chosen collar, $M$ a compact smooth manifold, and $E\to M$ a finite-rank smooth real vector bundle. Let $s:X\times M\to E$ be a continuous family of sections, meaning $s(x,m)\in E_m$ and $(x,m)\mapsto s(x,m)$ is continuous. Use the standard unitary representation of $SU(N)$ on $\mathbb C^N$ and the invariant positive inner product $\langle X,Y\rangle=-\operatorname{tr}(XY)$ on $\mathfrak{su}(N)$. Define the adjoint vector bundle $\operatorname{ad}P=P\times_{\operatorname{Ad}}\mathfrak{su}(N)$ and the adjoint group bundle $\operatorname{Ad}P=P\times_{\operatorname{Ad}}SU(N)$ with associated-bundle relation $[pg,z]=[p,\operatorname{Ad}_g z]$.

Choose one finite smooth bundle atlas with relatively compact coordinate domains and a subordinate partition of unity. For each integer $k>d/2+1$, let $H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$ and $H^{k+1}(\operatorname{ad}P)$ be the Sobolev completions of smooth sections in the resulting finite-atlas norms. Define the affine configuration space $\mathcal A_k:=A_0+H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$ and the set $\mathcal G_{k+1}:=H^{k+1}(\operatorname{Ad}P)$ of Sobolev gauge sections. The next lemma proves that the pointwise product and inverse close on this set and make it a Hilbert Lie group. Its based subset is $\mathcal G_{k+1,m}:=\{u\in\mathcal G_{k+1}:u(p_m)=e\}$. Let $Z_N=\{zI_N:z^N=1\}$ be the center of $SU(N)$, viewed as constant gauge sections. Indeed, if $Z=(z_{ij})$ is central and $D=\operatorname{diag}(t_1,\ldots,t_N)\in SU(N)$, then $(t_j-t_i)z_{ij}=0$. For each $i\ne j$ one can choose such a diagonal matrix with $t_i\ne t_j$, so $Z$ is diagonal. Commuting with the determinant-one unitary rotation whose block on the $(i,j)$ coordinates is $\begin{pmatrix}\cos t&\sin t\\-\sin t&\cos t\end{pmatrix}$ for $t\notin\pi\mathbb Z$ forces the $i$th and $j$th diagonal entries equal. Hence $Z=zI_N$; determinant one gives $z^N=1$, and conversely every such scalar is central. Write $\bar{\mathcal G}_{k+1}$ for the set of $Z_N$-cosets with quotient topology; the next lemma also verifies that the induced pointwise operation makes it a Hilbert Lie group.

Let $\mathcal A_\infty:=A_0+\Omega^1(M,\operatorname{ad}P)$ and let $\mathcal G_\infty$ be the smooth gauge group, with the $C^\infty$ section topology generated by all finite-atlas derivative seminorms. Define $\bar{\mathcal G}_\infty:=\mathcal G_\infty/Z_N$. In a local section of $P$, write a connection as a matrix-valued one-form $A$ and a gauge section as a map $u$ into $SU(N)$; the right gauge action is $A^u:=u^{-1}Au+u^{-1}du$, equivalently pullback by the gauge automorphism associated with $u$. The calculus lemma proves that this formula defines a smooth action on the Sobolev spaces above. For an adjoint section $\xi$, set $d_A\xi:=d\xi+[A,\xi]$ using the degree-one Lie-algebra-valued-form bracket. In local coordinates and an orthonormal adjoint frame, define the formal adjoint on an adjoint-valued one-form $a$ by $(d_A^*a)=-g^{ij}(\nabla_i^{\mathrm{LC}}a_j+[A_i,a_j])$, where $\nabla^{\mathrm{LC}}$ differentiates the covector index. This is the $L^2$ adjoint for the Riemannian volume and stated fiber metric; its local coefficient formula defines a distribution at Sobolev regularity.

For $A\in\mathcal A_k$, parallel transport of its $C^1$ connection form around piecewise smooth loops based at $p_m$ defines a subgroup $\operatorname{Hol}_{p_m}(A)\subseteq SU(N)$. Call $A$ irreducible when this subgroup leaves no nonzero proper complex subspace of $\mathbb C^N$ invariant; changing the chosen frame conjugates the subgroup and leaves this condition unchanged. Write $\mathcal A_k^*$ and $\mathcal A_\infty^*$ for the irreducible loci. Once the calculus lemma verifies the group action, define orbit equivalence by $A\sim B$ exactly when $B=A^u$ for some gauge section $u$; all resulting quotients carry the quotient topology, whose open sets are those with open inverse image under the orbit projection.

A **locally trivial fiber bundle with fiber $F$** is a continuous map $p:E\to B$, an open cover $(U_i)_{i\in S}$ of $B$, and homeomorphisms
$$\theta_i:p^{-1}(U_i)\longrightarrow U_i\times F,\qquad \operatorname{pr}_1\theta_i=p|_{p^{-1}(U_i)}.$$
Here bundle charts, including those used later for principal and associated bundles, are charts in ordinary topological spaces with ordinary product and subspace topologies. A bundle whose spaces are CGWH in addition can be considered in the CGWH fibration convention; we do not silently replace an ordinary product chart by a weaker k-product-chart assumption. Products and homeomorphisms have the meanings of [[thm-product-universal-property]] and [[def-homeomorphism-and-open-maps]].

On $U_i\cap U_j$, the coordinate change has the form $(b,x)\mapsto(b,g_{ji}(b,x))$, with continuous inverse $(b,y)\mapsto(b,g_{ij}(b,y))$. In particular each $g_{ji}(b,-)$ is a homeomorphism of $F$. The identities $g_{ii}(b,x)=x$ and $g_{ki}(b,x)=g_{kj}(b,g_{ji}(b,x))$ hold because the corresponding chart composites cancel. No topology on a homeomorphism group of $F$ is assumed.

The bundle is **numerable** when the data include a partition $(\rho_i:B\to[0,1])_{i\in S}$ with locally finite cozero sets, sum one, and
$$\operatorname{supp}(\rho_i)=\overline{\{b:\rho_i(b)>0\}}\subseteq U_i.$$
This is the support-subordinate convention of [[def-partition-of-unity-subordinate-to-a-cover]]. Repeating a chart with multiple indices is allowed, so a partition subordinate to a refinement can be accompanied by an explicitly assigned original chart. Merely having pointwise finite sums or cozero containment is not this specified numerating data.

An empty base forces $E$ empty and allows the empty cover and partition. The fiber $F$ may be empty: then every chart domain, hence $E$, is empty even when $B$ is nonempty. When $F$ is nonempty the charts imply surjectivity by taking one point in the chart fiber for each particular base point; this assertion does not require choosing a simultaneous section. Over a point a chart identifies $E$ with $F$. No AC is assumed in the definition.

Assume AC. Every numerable fiber bundle, with its supplied ordinary local product charts and support-subordinate locally finite partition of unity, is a Hurewicz fibration in all ordinary spaces. In particular a bundle of CGWH spaces with these charts is a Hurewicz fibration in CGWH. AC is used to well-order the set of finite chart words. No selection of a chart for every base point or of a separate lift for every path is made.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

For a based Serre fibration $p:(E,e_0)\to(B,b_0)$ with fiber $F=p^{-1}(b_0)$, the sequence
$$\cdots\to\pi_n(F)\xrightarrow{i_*}\pi_n(E)\xrightarrow{p_*}\pi_n(B)\xrightarrow{\partial_p}\pi_{n-1}(F)\to\cdots\to\pi_1(B)\xrightarrow{\partial_p}\pi_0(F)\xrightarrow{i_*}\pi_0(E)\xrightarrow{p_*}\pi_0(B)$$
is exact wherever there is an incoming and outgoing arrow. Basepoints are $e_0,b_0$ as appropriate. Exactness means incoming image equals the inverse image of the distinguished element. Arrows are homomorphisms where both group structures are defined; the component terms are pointed sets. The last arrow is onto precisely when $p(E)$ meets every path component of $B$.

There is a right action of $\pi_1(B,b_0)$ on $\pi_0(F)$: $[e]\cdot[\gamma]$ is the endpoint component of a lift of $\gamma$ starting at $e$, with loop products traversed left-to-right. Its orbits are precisely the fibers of $i_*:\pi_0(F)\to\pi_0(E)$, and the stabilizer of $[e_0]$ is $p_*\pi_1(E,e_0)$. Our boundary convention gives $\partial_p[\gamma]=[e_0]\cdot[\gamma]^{-1}$. These assertions require no AC.

For each integer $N\ge2$, let $SU(N)=\{U\in M_N(\mathbb C):U^*U=I,\det U=1\}$ and let $p:SU(N)\to S^{2N-1}\subset\mathbb C^N$ send a matrix to its last column. Then $p$ is a smooth, locally trivial fiber bundle with fiber $SU(N-1)$ over the last standard basis vector; for $N=2$, the fiber is the one-point group $SU(1)$.
For $n\ge2$, the unit sphere $S^{n-1}\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ is path-connected and connected.
Let $p:E\to B$ be a covering, $H:Y\times I\to B$ a homotopy, and $\widetilde H_0:Y\to E$ a lift of $H(-,0)$. There is a unique lift $\widetilde H:Y\times I\to E$ of $H$ extending $\widetilde H_0$.

derivations.claim: In a trivializing ball around $m$, choose a smooth bump $b$ supported in that ball with $b(m)=1$. For $g$ near $I$, use a smooth logarithm $X=\log g\in\mathfrak{su}(N)$ and define a gauge section by $u_g(x)=\exp(b(x)X)$ in that chart and the identity outside. This gives a continuous local section of evaluation near $I$. To see that every value is attained, begin at $N=2$: [F4] gives a bundle $SU(1)\to SU(2)\to S^3$ with one-point fiber, and [F5] makes the base path connected; the component exactness [F3] therefore makes $SU(2)$ path connected. Inductively, [F4] is a surjective locally trivial bundle with path-connected fiber $SU(N-1)$ and path-connected base sphere [F5]; path lifting and [F3] imply $SU(N)$ is path connected. A path from $I$ to any $g_0$ is covered by finitely many logarithm neighborhoods; subdividing it writes $g_0$ as a finite product of elements in the identity chart. Multiplying the corresponding bump-supported sections gives a gauge section $v_0$ with $v_0(p_m)=g_0$. Translation of the identity-neighborhood section by $v_0$ yields a local section near every $g_0$.

The finite group $Z_N$ acts on the Hausdorff topological group $\mathcal G(P)$ by free translations. Choose an identity neighborhood $V$ with $V^{-1}V\cap Z_N=\{e\}$; this is possible because the finite set $Z_N\setminus\{e\}$ is closed and avoids the identity. The translates $Vz$ are pairwise disjoint. Since the quotient map is open and identifies each translate homeomorphically with the image of $V$, that image is evenly covered. Translation gives the same construction around every group element, so the quotient map is a covering with exactly $|Z_N|=N$ sheets. By [F1] and [A1], this is the finite-center quotient specified in the Statement.

In the finite-atlas $C^\infty$ topology, pointwise multiplication and inversion are continuous: each derivative seminorm of a product or inverse is bounded on compact chart supports by finitely many derivative seminorms of the inputs, by the finite-dimensional product and chain rules. If $s:U\to\mathcal G(P)$ is one of the local sections, the maps
$$(v,g)\longmapsto v\,s(g),\qquad u\longmapsto\bigl(u\,s(ev_m(u))^{-1},ev_m(u)\bigr)$$
are continuous inverses between $\mathcal G_m(P)\times U$ and $ev_m^{-1}(U)$. The first coordinate in the inverse evaluates to $e$, and the product reconstructs $u$. Thus evaluation is a locally trivial bundle with fiber exactly its kernel $\mathcal G_m(P)$. A finite cover of compact $SU(N)$ by such neighborhoods and a partition of unity make this bundle numerable. By [F2] it is a Hurewicz fibration; [F3] supplies its homotopy LES.

The base $SU(N)$ is compact, so the finite local trivializations of evaluation admit a subordinate partition of unity. By [F2, F3] the evaluation bundle is a Serre fibration with the homotopy LES. The finite quotient is a covering; [F6] gives its homotopy lifting property and hence its fibration property. This completes the claims.

A **locally trivial fiber bundle with fiber $F$** is a continuous map $p:E\to B$, an open cover $(U_i)_{i\in S}$ of $B$, and homeomorphisms
$$\theta_i:p^{-1}(U_i)\longrightarrow U_i\times F,\qquad \operatorname{pr}_1\theta_i=p|_{p^{-1}(U_i)}.$$
Here bundle charts, including those used later for principal and associated bundles, are charts in ordinary topological spaces with ordinary product and subspace topologies. A bundle whose spaces are CGWH in addition can be considered in the CGWH fibration convention; we do not silently replace an ordinary product chart by a weaker k-product-chart assumption. Products and homeomorphisms have the meanings of [[thm-product-universal-property]] and [[def-homeomorphism-and-open-maps]].

On $U_i\cap U_j$, the coordinate change has the form $(b,x)\mapsto(b,g_{ji}(b,x))$, with continuous inverse $(b,y)\mapsto(b,g_{ij}(b,y))$. In particular each $g_{ji}(b,-)$ is a homeomorphism of $F$. The identities $g_{ii}(b,x)=x$ and $g_{ki}(b,x)=g_{kj}(b,g_{ji}(b,x))$ hold because the corresponding chart composites cancel. No topology on a homeomorphism group of $F$ is assumed.

The bundle is **numerable** when the data include a partition $(\rho_i:B\to[0,1])_{i\in S}$ with locally finite cozero sets, sum one, and
$$\operatorname{supp}(\rho_i)=\overline{\{b:\rho_i(b)>0\}}\subseteq U_i.$$
This is the support-subordinate convention of [[def-partition-of-unity-subordinate-to-a-cover]]. Repeating a chart with multiple indices is allowed, so a partition subordinate to a refinement can be accompanied by an explicitly assigned original chart. Merely having pointwise finite sums or cozero containment is not this specified numerating data.

An empty base forces $E$ empty and allows the empty cover and partition. The fiber $F$ may be empty: then every chart domain, hence $E$, is empty even when $B$ is nonempty. When $F$ is nonempty the charts imply surjectivity by taking one point in the chart fiber for each particular base point; this assertion does not require choosing a simultaneous section. Over a point a chart identifies $E$ with $F$. No AC is assumed in the definition.

A based map $f:(X,x_0)\to(Y,y_0)$ induces $f_*[a]=[f\circ a]$ on all pointed component and cubical homotopy sets. For $n\ge1$ this is a homomorphism, identities and composition are preserved, and based homotopic maps induce equal maps. Based homotopy equivalences induce isomorphisms.
